video_title: Tuomas Iisalo Press Conference | Grizzlies vs. Warriors

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo on Grizzlies' defensive improvements in second half
quotes.excerpt: our guys did a tremendous job in the second half then doing much better job not fouling
quotes.quote: I thought especially the first half I had a very divided opinion about the possessions we had because I thought we played some of the best disruption we have had in a long time. We were getting a lot of deflections, we were executing our pick-and-roll coverage. Guys looked very good, moving very well with their feet. And then there were a couple of things in the first half that we did a poor job of, so there was a huge contrast. We allowed guys to get to their strong hand all the way to the rim, we put them on the free-throw line, and we gave them second-shot opportunities. You can imagine what the outcome is going to be in NBA games if you allow guys right-hand layups, free throws, and then five to ten shots more. Usually the outcome is going to be very bad. So that was the main thing in the first half, and I think our guys did a tremendous job in the second half then doing much better job not fouling, keeping them off their strong hand, and the rebounding stayed as an issue, but we on the other hand were able to force some turnovers and negate that rebounding differential.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo says the Grizzlies defensive focus in the second half was key to their success, specifically noting the team did a better job keeping opponents off their strong hand and avoiding unnecessary fouls.

structured.context: Head coach Tuomas Iisalo discusses the Grizzlies' defensive performance and adjustments made during the game against the Warriors.

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo on the importance of playoff experience for young teams
quotes.excerpt: it's such a luxury for young teams to get those get reps in in the tight games
quotes.quote: What we have also spoken about that eventually at some point this group hopefully will play in the playoffs. And there, you have one day in between the games, time to make those adjustments, and then you got to get your body to execute it also on the court. And you only get better at it if you are put in the situations where you actually get to practice that. And that's why it's such a luxury for young teams to get those get reps in in the tight games that we have had that we have spoken about also this season, different time and score scenarios. It's also very important to have success early on as a group so that you can get to those games, whether it's play-ins or playoffs, for the players to get experience of that.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo emphasizes the importance of young teams getting reps in tight game scenarios, noting that experiencing different time and score situations is a luxury that prepares players for the playoffs.

structured.context: Tuomas Iisalo explains the importance of high-pressure game situations and playoff experience for the development of his young team.

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo on Cam Boozer's development and decision-making
quotes.excerpt: he's starting to figure it out and his big strength really is taking what the game gives him
quotes.quote: He's starting to figure it out and his big strength really is taking what the game gives him. And I think he's been better at it. Also the guys around him are playing better, so he's part of a lot of these functional lineups where you have five guys playing with a lot of confidence and then it becomes also easier for him to feed the other guys because he knows something's going to happen. But I think it's a lot about that and you saw in Washington for example, they were sagging off of him, everybody still keeps feeding him, he keeps taking those shots and I think he went seven for eight after missing the first five. That speaks a lot about his character.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo praises Cam Boozer for his character and decision making, noting that his ability to keep shooting after a slow start shows exactly what kind of player he is becoming.

structured.context: Tuomas Iisalo evaluates the recent growth and decision-making of Cam Boozer within the team's offensive system.

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo provides update on Jeremy's calf injury
quotes.excerpt: no indication yet on the severity, he will get the imaging done tomorrow
quotes.quote: No indication yet on the severity. He will get the imaging done tomorrow. The good news is that it's the calf that's injured and nothing else.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo says there is no update yet on the severity of Jeremy's calf injury. He will undergo imaging tomorrow.

structured.context: Tuomas Iisalo provides an update on the status of Jeremy following a calf injury sustained during the game.

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo on Cedric Coward and Jaylen Wells' complementary skills
quotes.excerpt: both guys have high ambitions about what and who they want to be as basketball players
quotes.quote: Both guys have high ambitions about what and who they want to be as basketball players, but they're not using the team as a platform for self-development in that regard that they would put themselves above the team. And I think there's been discussions about Cedric should do this or Cedric should do that. Cedric's leading our team in the on-offs exactly because he makes a lot of the right plays on the right time. He's aggressive in the right time, he's patient. And I think a lot of times these young players, the advice or the general narrative can be extremely misleading. And that's one of those things where then helps to have good relationships with the players and obviously helps to win because you see then everybody benefits from that.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo pushes back on external narratives regarding Cedric Coward, saying he is leading the team in on-offs because he makes the right plays at the right time rather than putting himself above the team.

structured.context: Tuomas Iisalo discusses the selfless play and development of Cedric Coward and Jaylen Wells within the team structure.

quotes.speaker: Tuomas Iisalo
quotes.summary_phrase: Tuomas Iisalo on the value of end-of-season reps for young players
quotes.excerpt: they have developed as individual players, they've physically developed, they've developed technically
quotes.quote: They have developed as individual players, they've physically developed, they've developed technically, they've improved their individual tactical understanding about the game of basketball, what to do in this situation. You see some a lot of defensive stuff, but I would say the biggest thing in that we did not give up on this at the end of the season was to try to practice and try to develop this group and sometimes I felt it wasn't easy. We were losing games and at the same time we're trying to still look to develop this group but what they do really well and you see it right now, they are fluent in our language, they're fluent in our on-court language, they speak the same language.
quotes.social_post: Tuomas Iisalo credits the growth of his young roster to their commitment to development even during a tough season, noting that the group is now fluent in the teams on-court language.

structured.context: Tuomas Iisalo reflects on the team's collective growth and improved communication throughout the final stretch of the season.
